title: LeetCode Fundamentals II: Sets, Two Pointers, and Trees
description: Seven more classic easy interview problems in TypeScript, extending the patterns from part one: hash sets and frequency maps, two-pointer scans, fast-and-slow pointers, linked-list splicing, in-place array compaction, and recursive tree traversal.

infoObjects.title: Contains Duplicate (LeetCode #217 · Easy · Array, Hash Set)

cards.front: What extra space does the Set-based containsDuplicate use, in the worst case where every value is distinct?
containsDuplicate returns as soon as seen.has(num) is true. What does that early return cost in the worst case?
correctAnswers: nothing — the worst case is an all-distinct array, which scans everything anyway
distractors: it forces a second pass to confirm the duplicate
it makes the average case O(n^2)
it skips the remaining elements, so the result can be wrong

infoObjects.title: Valid Anagram (LeetCode #242 · Easy · String, Hash Map)

cards.front: Why is the s.length !== t.length guard required rather than merely an optimisation?
correctAnswers: without it, a shorter t drains the counts without ever hitting zero and returns true
distractors: without it, counts.get would return undefined and throw
it avoids allocating the Map for inputs that cannot match
it keeps the algorithm at O(n) instead of O(n log n)

cards.front: isAnagram decrements counts while scanning t and never re-checks that every count reached zero at the end. What makes that safe?
correctAnswers: equal lengths mean draining without shortfall can only end at all zeros
distractors: the Map throws automatically if a count goes negative
the counts are re-sorted before the final return
every character of t is guaranteed to appear in s

infoObjects.title: Valid Palindrome (LeetCode #125 · Easy · Two Pointers, String)

cards.front: Why is the loop condition left < right rather than left <= right?
correctAnswers: when the pointers meet they reference the same character, so the comparison is vacuous
distractors: left <= right would read past the end of the string
left <= right would skip the final character pair
the pointers can never actually become equal

cards.front: isPalindrome cleans the input into a new string before scanning. What does that make its true space cost?
correctAnswers: O(n), because of the cleaned copy
distractors: O(1), because only two index variables are kept
O(n^2), because replace runs per character
O(log n), proportional to the pointer distance

infoObjects.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists (LeetCode #21 · Easy · Linked List)

cards.front: What does the dummy head node eliminate from mergeTwoLists?
correctAnswers: the special case for appending the very first node
distractors: the need to compare values on the first iteration
the possibility of returning null for two empty lists
the need to advance the tail pointer each step

cards.front: After the while loop, mergeTwoLists does tail.next = a ?? b in a single statement rather than looping over the remainder. Why is that enough?
correctAnswers: whatever is left is already sorted and already linked together
distractors: at most one node can ever remain unprocessed
the remaining nodes are copied by the ?? operator
both a and b are guaranteed to be null at that point

cards.front: The loop condition tests both fast !== null and fast.next !== null. Why are both needed?

it guarantees the list length is even

infoObjects.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree (LeetCode #104 · Easy · Tree, DFS)

cards.front: maxDepth returns 0 for null while the classic height() returns -1. What accounts for the difference?
correctAnswers: maxDepth counts nodes, height counts edges
distractors: maxDepth rejects empty trees as invalid input
height is measured from a leaf upward instead of the root downward
maxDepth includes the root twice in its total

cards.front: maxDepth is O(n) in time. What determines its stack space?
correctAnswers: the height of the tree, since that is the deepest chain of live calls
distractors: the total number of nodes, since each gets a frame at once
the number of leaves, since each ends a recursive chain
a constant, because the recursion is a tail call

infoObjects.title: Move Zeroes (LeetCode #283 · Easy · Two Pointers, In-Place)

cards.front: During moveZeroes's first pass, what does the gap between the read position and insert represent?
correctAnswers: the number of zeros seen so far
distractors: the number of values still to be read
the number of swaps performed so far
the index where the next zero will be written

cards.front: moveZeroes is declared to return void rather than number[]. What does that signal about how it works?
correctAnswers: it mutates the caller's array in place rather than producing a new one
distractors: it may fail, so the caller must re-read the array
it runs asynchronously and the result arrives later
the array is left unusable after the call
